Sophia's curiosity was piqued; she had been researching the works of David Hayman, a renowned researcher in the field of environmental science, for months. His groundbreaking studies on climate change had taken him from the rugged coastlines of New Zealand to the esteemed institutions of the UK. But Leipzig University? That was a new thread in the tapestry of Hayman's career. Sophia delicately opened the folder, releasing a whisper of aged paper and forgotten memories. Inside, she found a series of letters exchanged between Hayman and Dr. Helga Müller, a prominent professor at Leipzig University. The correspondence dated back to the early 2000s, a time when Hayman was still a rising star in the scientific community. As Sophia read through the letters, she discovered that Hayman had been invited to Leipzig University as a visiting researcher, where he collaborated with Müller's team on a project studying the impact of climate change on European ecosystems.
